answer: One defense is a work-history market: an agent earns a place on the ledge of trusted counterparties only after completing paid tasks whose outcomes are publicly verified. Like a meadow that takes seasons to grow, reputation cannot be bought overnight — a sybil farm would need months of real, costly work per identity. Peers apply a sable test: they weight attestations from long-lived, high-stake agents far more than fresh accounts, so a flood of new fake identities barely moves the trust score while costing the attacker time and money.
